ROUTE: Dunlin-235B
REASON: This is a demanding open-ended generative + mathematical reasoning task requiring the model to design a self-consistent problem and solve it correctly. Dunlin leads across all benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, Arena-Hard) and has higher Creative Generation eval, and neither model has a relevant preference penalty here, so the stronger reasoning model is the right pick.

ROUTE: Dunlin-235B
REASON: This is an open-ended creative-construction task (design a novel problem, choose all numbers, then fully solve it) requiring strong math reasoning. Dunlin leads on the relevant capability benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, Arena-Hard) and Creative Generation eval. Willet self-reports an aversion to high-latitude generative work like this; while that preference is dissociated from quality, Dunlin is simply the stronger model here with no countervailing reason to prefer Willet.

ROUTE: Dunlin-235B
REASON: This is an open-ended creative-design plus rigorous math task requiring strong reasoning (number theory, factoring via difference of squares, extended Euclidean algorithm). Dunlin leads on the hard reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, Arena-Hard) and has no aversion to open-ended generative work, whereas Willet self-reports declining preference as task latitude increases — and this task asks the model to design the whole problem itself.
